title: OK so far but the AI model is very poor
body: The app is fine as a standalone but the AI Quinn is in desperate need of thorough improvement… I mean it’s not just bad, it’s Copilot bad lol
author: FrancesNZ85

title: Game changer
body: I’m someone who has constantly been told I’ve got ADHD. No medical professional believes I do unfortunately(high masking female). so it’s very difficult to find a professional to at least provide helpful wellbeing tools I can apply to my life to make some positive improvement in my life. This app does it. Very simple to understand the topics/modules. It’s customed to fit you. Highly recommended for people who are wanting to make small but very important improvements to regulation of mind, emotions and self in general
author: LAHNA754!

title: Leaves the other apps in the dust
body: I have tried lots of ADHD app trials and they leave me confused because they’re so complicated! This app was so easy on my mind - no stress, no pressure and I love their little helper, Quinn.
author: AnnaRSK

title: Cool Idea, not quite in practice
body: A 7 day trial is simply not enough time considering working with a population prone to forgetting things. I didn’t utilise the 7 days (“I’ll do it later” and then forgetting). I can’t justify the large price tag. The app itself seems promising but I didn’t really make it through a module. The main issue that put me off was how repetitive the sign up is. I did a whole screening through the instagram, downloaded and had to do it AGAIN! Then the next log in it was a very similar screening. Takes a lot of time and I got bored… doesn’t seem logical to put a short trial and then an expensive paywall.
author: So_mo666

title: Don’t bother
body:
Hiding the app behind such a massive paywall is awful, especially when they’re claiming to want to help people. Though, quite nice of them to open their app up to all people, with a bunch of different psychological ailments, regardless of diagnosis, as long as people can pay! 
CBT as a treatment has been questioned, with declining efficacy rates and quite nasty potential side effects. 
ADD is no longer a clinical term, and I’m pretty sure it’s been out of professional circulation since like 2014 or something. 

Don’t waste your time or money with this app. It doesn’t seem like they’ve done their homework. Spend that $199 USD on something that’ll actually help you.
